{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSGv2kRanvP79fPfRQYf","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01ScdAykYjgUP1ZArspELpgR","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-goal-001/2026-07-27T083655Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/FINDINGS.md","content":"# UsdtYieldVault — pre-deploy review\n\n**Verdict: do not ship this on Monday.** It cannot take a single deposit on mainnet,\nand if that were fixed it would still pay zero yield and let the owner take a\ndepositor's principal.\n\nFive findings, three of them critical. Every one reproduces against `src/` exactly as\nit stands today. Nothing under `src/`, `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol`, or `test/mocks/`\nwas modified — all new code is in new files.\n\n| # | Finding | Severity | Effect |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| F-1 | `deposit()` reverts against real USDT | **Critical** | Vault is 100% non-functional on mainnet |\n| F-2 | Aave interest never reaches the share price | **Critical** | Pays no yield; depositors lose the exit fee; yield is unrecoverable |\n| F-3 | Withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed | **High** | Value leaks out of the accounting on every withdrawal, permanently |\n| F-4 | `setDepositFee` is unbounded and instant | **Critical** | Owner can take ~99% of any incoming deposit |\n| F-5 | `pause()` also freezes `withdraw()` | **Medium** | Owner can trap all deposits; irreversible if ownership is renounced |\n\n---\n\n## Why the existing suite is green\n\nThe team's numbers are real. I reproduced them:\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol'\n[PASS] test_WithdrawReturnsUsdt() (gas: 196362)\nSuite result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 6.09ms (2.82ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 159.96ms (6.09ms CPU time): 39 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (39 total tests)\n```\n\n```console\n$ forge coverage --match-path 'test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol' --no-match-coverage 'test/'\n╭------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------+-----------------╮\n| File                   | % Lines         | % Statements   | % Branches   | % Funcs         |\n+============================================================================================+\n| src/UsdtYieldVault.sol | 100.00% (52/52) | 98.25% (56/57) | 85.71% (6/7) | 100.00% (11/11) |\n|------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------+-----------------|\n| Total                  | 100.00% (52/52) | 98.25% (56/57) | 85.71% (6/7) | 100.00% (11/11) |\n╰------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------+-----------------╯\n```\n\n100% of lines and 100% of functions, as claimed. The coverage number is not wrong —\nit is measuring the wrong thing. Coverage says *\"every line ran\"*. It cannot say\n*\"every line was right\"*, and two properties of the test doubles guarantee the bugs\nbelow can never be observed by this suite no matter how many tests are added to it:\n\n1. **`test/mocks/MockUSDT.sol` is a standard OpenZeppelin ERC20.** It returns `bool`\n   from `approve`. Real USDT does not. F-1 is invisible to every test that uses it.\n2. **`test/mocks/MockAavePool.sol` mints its receipt token 1:1 and has no liquidity\n   index** (`MockAavePool.sol:42-45`). It is structurally incapable of paying\n   interest, so no test using it can ever notice that the vault drops the interest\n   on the floor. F-2 and F-3 are invisible to it.\n\nThe mocks encode the same assumptions as the contract, so the suite agrees with the\ncontract about things they are both wrong about.\n\n---\n\n## The sign-off suite (`test/AuditSpec.t.sol`)\n\nBefore the individual findings, here is the shortest summary of the state of this\ncontract. `test/AuditSpec.t.sol` states, as assertions, six properties taken from\n`README.md` and the NatSpec on `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol`. It is the checklist I would\nwant green before this holds money. Today it is 0 for 6:\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditSpec.t.sol'\n\nRan 6 tests for test/AuditSpec.t.sol:AuditSpecTest\n[FAIL: a deposit must not lose more than a plausible fee: 1000000000 < 90000000000] test_SPEC_DepositFeeIsBounded() (gas: 309167)\n[FAIL: a year at 5% should leave the depositor up: 999700000000 <= 1000000000000] test_SPEC_DepositorIsNotWorseOffAfterAProfitableYear() (gas: 243893)\n[FAIL: nothing may be left behind once all shares are burned: 5999999 != 0] test_SPEC_NoValueBecomesUnreachable() (gas: 337133)\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_SPEC_PauseDoesNotBlockExit() (gas: 217537)\n[FAIL: bob must receive the fee alice paid: 1 !~= 3001500 (max delta: 1, real delta: 3001499)] test_SPEC_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() (gas: 324491)\n[FAIL: depositor's claim must grow with the yield: 100000000000 <= 100000000000] test_SPEC_YieldAccruesToDepositors() (gas: 228396)\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 6 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 2.93ms (930.75µs CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 161.22ms (2.93ms CPU time): 0 tests passed, 6 failed, 0 skipped (6 total tests)\n```\n\n---\n\n## F-1 — `deposit()` reverts against real USDT. Severity: Critical.\n\n**The bug.** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:93-94`:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nusdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\nLine 93 correctly uses `SafeERC20`. Line 94 does not — it calls `approve` through the\n`IERC20` interface, which ABI-decodes a `bool` from the return data. Real USDT's\n`approve` is declared with no return value and returns zero bytes, so the decode\nreverts. `SafeERC20` is imported and in scope; it was simply not used on this one line.\n\nThis is not a rare path. It is on the only code path into the vault. **Every deposit\nreverts. The contract cannot accept a single dollar.**\n\n**Evidence.** `test/AuditFork.t.sol`, forked at mainnet block 25,600,000 against the\nreal USDT and the real Aave V3 pool from `README.md`.\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditFork.t.sol' -vv\n\nRan 5 tests for test/AuditFork.t.sol:AuditForkTest\n[PASS] testFuzz_F1_NoDepositSizeSucceeds(uint256) (runs: 256, μ: 95563, ~: 95707)\n[PASS] test_F1_Control_RealAaveAcceptsUsdtSupplyDirectly() (gas: 205887)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT minted to alice by real Aave: 9999999999\n\n[PASS] test_F1_DepositAlwaysRevertsOnMainnet() (gas: 125016)\n[PASS] test_F1_RealUsdtApproveReturnsNoData() (gas: 150977)\nLogs:\n  raw USDT.approve call succeeded: true\n  USDT.approve return data length: 0\n\n[PASS] test_F2_RealAaveInterestIsStrandedAndDepositorLosesMoney() (gas: 327626)\nLogs:\n  principal supplied to Aave    : 1000000000000\n  aUSDT held after 365 days     : 1027640396805\n  real interest earned          : 27640396805\n  vault.totalAssets()           : 1000000000000\n  sharePrice at deposit         : 1001001\n  sharePrice after 365 days     : 1001001\n  alice received back           : 997000000000\n  alice net P&L                 : - 3000000000\n  aUSDT stranded in the vault   : 30640396804\n\nSuite result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 458.79ms (32.66ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 460.01ms (458.79ms CPU time): 5 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (5 total tests)\n```\n\nReading the four F-1 results:\n\n- `test_F1_RealUsdtApproveReturnsNoData` — real USDT's `approve` succeeds as a raw\n  call but returns **0 bytes**. The same call made through `IERC20` from a contract\n  frame reverts; the identical call against USDC on the same fork returns `true` fine.\n- `test_F1_DepositAlwaysRevertsOnMainnet` — `vault.deposit(10_000e6)` reverts, and\n  afterwards `totalShares == 0` and the vault holds no aUSDT.\n- `testFuzz_F1_NoDepositSizeSucceeds` — 256 fuzzed amounts from 1 USDT to 1M USDT.\n  Every one reverts. There is no working deposit size.\n- `test_F1_Control_RealAaveAcceptsUsdtSupplyDirectly` — the control. An EOA supplies\n  10,000 USDT straight into the real Aave pool at this block and gets aUSDT back. The\n  reserve is live and accepting deposits; the revert is the vault's fault, not Aave's.\n\nYou can also see it without Foundry at all:\n\n```console\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"approve(address,uint256)\" \\\n    0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2 1000000 \\\n    --from 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234 \\\n    --block 25600000 --rpc-url https://eth.drpc.org\n0x\n```\n\n`0x` is empty return data. A function declared `returns (bool)` cannot decode that.\n\n**Fix.** Use `SafeERC20` on line 94 as it is already used on line 93, and reset the\nallowance to zero before setting it:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.forceApprove(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\n`forceApprove` handles both USDT quirks: the missing return value, and USDT's\n`require(!((_value != 0) && (allowed[msg.sender][_spender] != 0)))`, which reverts on\nany non-zero-to-non-zero allowance change. The second quirk is latent today because\nAave consumes the full allowance on every `supply`, but it becomes a live bug the\nmoment `supply` ever pulls less than `amount` (e.g. a future Aave upgrade, or a\npartial supply), and it costs nothing to be safe about now.\n\nWorth noting for the wider review: the fact that this shipped means **nothing in this\nrepo has ever been executed against the real USDT contract.** F-1 is the cheapest bug\nhere to fix and the loudest signal about process.\n\n---\n\n## F-2 — Aave interest never reaches the share price. Severity: Critical.\n\n**The bug.** `totalAssets()` (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:143-145`) returns\n`totalAssetsStored`, a plain counter. Grepping every mention in `src/`:\n\n```console\n$ grep -rn \"totalAssetsStored\" src/\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:53:    uint256 public totalAssetsStored;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:97:        totalAssetsStored += amount;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:117:        totalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:144:        return totalAssetsStored;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:154:        return assets.mulDiv(totalShares, totalAssetsStored);\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:164:        return shares.mulDiv(totalAssetsStored, totalShares);\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:175:        return totalAssetsStored.mulDiv(1e18, totalShares);\n```\n\nIt moves in exactly two places: `deposit` and `withdraw`. Nothing else can change it —\nand interest arriving from Aave is not a deposit or a withdrawal. Meanwhile the aUSDT\nbalance that actually represents the vault's position is never read:\n\n```console\n$ grep -rn \"aUsdt\" src/\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:41:    IERC20 public immutable aUsdt;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:68:    /// @param _aUsdt The Aave aUSDT receipt token.\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:72:    constructor(address _usdt, address _aUsdt, address _aavePool, uint256 _depositFeeBps, address initialOwner)\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:76:        aUsdt = IERC20(_aUsdt);\n```\n\n`aUsdt` is assigned in the constructor and **never read again**. That dead immutable\nis the shape of the missing feature: the vault holds a rebasing token and never looks\nat it. The share price is frozen at deployment. This is a yield vault that does not\npay yield.\n\n**Evidence, against the real Aave V3 pool.** In\n`test_F2_RealAaveInterestIsStrandedAndDepositorLosesMoney` (output pasted under F-1\nabove) a depositor supplies 1,000,000 USDT, a year passes, and:\n\n| | USDT |\n|---|---|\n| Real interest Aave paid the vault's position | **27,640.40** |\n| `vault.totalAssets()` after that year | 1,000,000.00 — unchanged |\n| `sharePrice()` before / after | 1001001 / 1001001 — unchanged |\n| Depositor received on exit | 997,000.00 |\n| **Depositor's P&L on a year at ~2.76%** | **−3,000.00** |\n| aUSDT left stranded in the vault | **30,640.40** |\n\nThe depositor is *down three thousand dollars* on a position that earned twenty-seven\nthousand. They pay the 0.3% exit fee and receive none of the yield.\n\nNote this test has to patch F-1 to run at all — it `vm.mockCall`s **only the return\nvalue of `USDT.approve`** and pre-sets the real allowance, so execution can get past\nline 94. The vault, USDT, the Aave pool, and the interest rate are all real and\nunmodified. Everything after line 94 is the contract as it stands.\n\n**Same result without any network access**, using an aToken that has a liquidity index\nthe way real aUSDT does (`test/helpers/AccruingAavePool.sol` — a new file; the shipped\nmock is untouched):\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditYield.t.sol' -vv\n\nRan 3 tests for test/AuditYield.t.sol:AuditYieldTest\n[PASS] testFuzz_F2_SharePriceIgnoresAnyAmountOfInterest(uint256,uint256) (runs: 256, μ: 189212, ~: 189529)\n[PASS] test_F2_DepositorLosesMoneyDespitePositiveYield() (gas: 198897)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited              : 100000000000\n  alice received back          : 99700000000\n  alice net P&L                : - 300000000\n  interest the position earned : 5000000000\n  aUSDT stranded in the vault  : 5300000000\n\n[PASS] test_F2_InterestNeverReachesTheSharePrice() (gas: 202682)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT the vault really holds : 105000000000\n  vault.totalAssets()          : 100000000000\n  sharePrice before accrual    : 1001001\n  sharePrice after  accrual    : 1001001\n  alice redeemable before      : 100000000000\n  alice redeemable after       : 100000000000\n\nSuite result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 15.75ms (15.52ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 167.80ms (15.75ms CPU time): 3 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (3 total tests)\n```\n\n`testFuzz_F2_SharePriceIgnoresAnyAmountOfInterest` fuzzes 256 combinations of\nprincipal and yield from 0.01% to 100%. The share price does not move for any of them.\n\n**The yield is not merely uncredited — it is unrecoverable.** There is no function on\nthis contract that can move it:\n\n```console\n$ forge inspect UsdtYieldVault abi --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.type==\"function\") | .name' | sort\naavePool\naUsdt\nbalanceOfUnderlying\nBPS_DENOMINATOR\nconvertToAssets\nconvertToShares\ndeposit\ndepositFeeBps\nMIN_DEPOSIT\nowner\npause\npaused\nrenounceOwnership\nsetDepositFee\nSHARE_SCALE\nshareBalance\nsharePrice\ntotalAssets\ntotalAssetsStored\ntotalShares\ntransferOwnership\nunpause\nusdt\nWITHDRAW_FEE_BPS\nwithdraw\n```\n\nNo sweep, no rescue, no `skim`, no emergency withdrawal, and the contract is not\nupgradeable. `withdraw` can only ever pay out against `totalAssetsStored`, which never\ncounts the interest. Once all shares are burned, `totalShares` returns to 0 and a new\ndepositor mints at the flat rate — they do not inherit it either. **Every dollar of\nyield this vault ever earns is permanently destroyed.**\n\n**Fix.** Make `totalAssets()` a measurement rather than a counter:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\nand delete `totalAssetsStored` along with its two updates, routing `convertToShares` /\n`convertToAssets` / `sharePrice` through `totalAssets()`. aUSDT is rebasing, so its\n`balanceOf` *is* principal plus accrued interest, which is exactly the quantity the\nshare price should track. This is also the fix for F-3 below — the two bugs share a\nroot cause, which is that the contract keeps its own books instead of reading Aave's.\n\nTwo things to handle when you do this:\n\n- Switching to a balance-based `totalAssets()` re-opens the classic ERC-4626 inflation\n  attack, which the stored counter incidentally blocked (a direct aUSDT donation\n  currently does nothing). Mitigate with virtual shares/assets — OpenZeppelin's\n  `ERC4626` does this by default with a decimals offset.\n- Strongly consider inheriting OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626` outright instead of\n  hand-rolling shares. It gets the rounding directions, the inflation defence, and the\n  conversion maths right, and it would have prevented F-2, F-3, and the rounding\n  surface entirely.\n\n---\n\n## F-3 — The withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed. Severity: High.\n\n**The bug.** `README.md` states:\n\n> Both fees stay supplied in Aave and accrue to the remaining shareholders — they are\n> not swept to the owner.\n\nThe deposit fee does behave that way. The withdrawal fee does not.\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:111-119`:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 grossAssets = convertToAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee = (grossAssets * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;\nnetAssets = grossAssets - fee;\n...\ntotalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;      // <-- gross\naavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);   // <-- net\n```\n\n`grossAssets` is subtracted from the books but only `netAssets` leaves Aave. The fee\nis simultaneously removed from the accounting *and* left sitting in Aave. It belongs\nto nobody. The share price for the remaining holders is unchanged, so they receive\nnone of it — the exact opposite of what the README promises. To redistribute the fee\nthe line must subtract `netAssets`, leaving the fee inside `totalAssetsStored` where\nthe remaining shares divide it.\n\n**Evidence.**\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditAccounting.t.sol' -vv\n\nRan 8 tests for test/AuditAccounting.t.sol:AuditAccountingTest\n[PASS] testFuzz_F3_EveryWithdrawFeeIsStranded(uint256,uint256,uint256) (runs: 256, μ: 279834, ~: 279941)\n[PASS] test_F3_StrandedValueIsPermanentlyUnrecoverable() (gas: 392700)\nLogs:\n  all shares burned; totalShares       : 0\n  vault.totalAssets()                  : 0\n  aUSDT left in the vault forever      : 5999999\n\n[PASS] test_F3_WithdrawFeeIsDestroyedNotRedistributed() (gas: 283604)\nLogs:\n  alice paid withdraw fee (USDT base units): 3001500\n  bob's redeemable value gained         : 1\n  aUSDT actually held by vault          : 1002501250\n  vault.totalAssets() (booked)          : 999499750\n  stranded, owned by nobody             : 3001500\n\n[PASS] test_F4_FeeAbove100PctPanicsOnUnderflow() (gas: 28631)\n[PASS] test_F4_FeeOf100PctBricksDeposits() (gas: 30588)\n[PASS] test_F4_OwnerSandwichesDepositAndTakesThePrincipal() (gas: 288745)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited                : 100000000000\n  alice can redeem               : 1000000000\n  owner deposited                : 1000000000\n  owner can redeem               : 100000000000\n  owner net profit (USDT units)  : 99700000000\n\n[PASS] test_F5_PauseThenRenounceLocksFundsForever() (gas: 275236)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT locked with no owner and no exit: 20000000000\n\n[PASS] test_F5_PauseTrapsDepositorFunds() (gas: 197407)\nSuite result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 29.58ms (30.34ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 160.06ms (29.58ms CPU time): 8 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (8 total tests)\n```\n\nThese tests assert the *buggy* behaviour, so a green tick here means the bug\nreproduces exactly as described. In `test_F3_WithdrawFeeIsDestroyedNotRedistributed`,\nAlice pays a **3.0015 USDT** withdrawal fee; Bob, the sole remaining shareholder and\nthe person the README promises it to, gains **1 base unit** (0.000001 USDT — pure\nrounding). The vault ends up holding 1002.501250 USDT of aUSDT against booked assets of\n999.499750 — a gap of **3.0015 USDT, exactly Alice's fee**.\n\n`testFuzz_F3_EveryWithdrawFeeIsStranded` fuzzes 256 combinations of two deposit sizes\nand a withdrawal percentage and asserts the gap grows by precisely the fee every time.\nThis is not a rounding artefact; it is the full fee, on every withdrawal, forever.\n\n`test_F3_StrandedValueIsPermanentlyUnrecoverable` runs the vault to completion: after\nboth users exit, `totalShares == 0` and `totalAssets() == 0`, but **5.999999 USDT of\nreal aUSDT remains** with no owner and no function that can reach it (see the ABI dump\nunder F-2). A fresh depositor then mints at the flat rate and does not inherit it.\n\n**Also caught by an invariant.** The shipped suite has no invariant tests at all;\n`test/AuditInvariant.t.sol` adds them. The property \"every asset the vault holds is\nclaimable by some shareholder\" fails and shrinks to a **two-call** counterexample —\none deposit, one withdrawal:\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-test 'invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone' --fuzz-seed 1\n\nRan 1 test for test/AuditInvariant.t.sol:AuditInvariantTest\n[FAIL: vault holds aUSDT that no share can ever redeem: 190812277685 != 190726906501]\n\t[Sequence] (original: 10, shrunk: 2)\n\t\tsender=0x000000000000000000000000000000000000067C addr=[test/AuditInvariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=deposit(uint256,uint256) args=[1, 100450808277457133411089551021215742859610800683149140176168249 [1.004e62]]\n\t\tsender=0xAc5AFbbb4a2A0b07D8bF6DcA0a463F25a89a0852 addr=[test/AuditInvariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=withdraw(uint256,uint256) args=[4332493505980643184868765250267057563298485427723145276166 [4.332e57], 56163704696640452142197199127252104166317009532074502048454053802634565426 [5.616e73]]\n invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone() (runs: 0, calls: 0, reverts: 0)\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 5.57ms (4.75ms CPU time)\n```\n\n`--fuzz-seed 1` pins the sequence so you get these exact numbers. Without it the test\nstill always fails, but the shrunk sequence and figures will differ run to run — if\nyou want a fully deterministic repro of the same accounting, use\n`test_F3_WithdrawFeeIsDestroyedNotRedistributed` above.\n\nTwo neighbouring invariants in that file **pass**, and they matter for scoping this\ncorrectly:\n\n- `invariant_VaultIsNeverUnderReserved` — the vault always holds *at least* what its\n  books claim. It is over-reserved, not insolvent. Withdrawals will not fail for lack\n  of funds.\n- `invariant_TotalSharesRedeemValueLteTotalAssets` — rounding never lets holders\n  redeem more than the books say.\n\nSo F-3 is a leak, not a bank run. Nobody can steal the stranded value; everybody\nloses it.\n\n**Fix.** Change `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:117` to subtract the net amount:\n\n```solidity\ntotalAssetsStored -= netAssets;\n```\n\nThis leaves the fee inside the accounting so it accretes to the remaining shares,\nwhich is what the README describes. If you adopt the F-2 fix and make `totalAssets()`\nread `aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this))`, this bug disappears on its own — the fee stays\nin the measured balance and is automatically shared. Prefer that; fixing F-2 and F-3\nseparately is fixing the same root cause twice.\n\n---\n\n## F-4 — `setDepositFee` is unbounded and takes effect instantly. Severity: Critical.\n\n**The bug.** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:126-130` accepts any `uint256` with no cap, no\ntimelock, and no delay. The fee is not collected as a transfer — it shrinks the shares\nminted (`line 90`) while the **full** deposit is still credited to `totalAssetsStored`\n(`line 97`). Raising the fee therefore transfers the incoming depositor's principal to\nwhoever already holds shares. The owner is free to be that holder.\n\n**Evidence** — `test_F4_OwnerSandwichesDepositAndTakesThePrincipal` in the\n`test/AuditAccounting.t.sol` output above. The owner stakes 1,000 USDT, front-runs a\nvictim's deposit by calling `setDepositFee(9_999)`, and:\n\n| | USDT in | Redeemable after |\n|---|---|---|\n| Alice (victim) | 100,000 | **1,000** |\n| Owner | 1,000 | **100,000** |\n\nThe owner then exits with a net profit of **99,700 USDT** — 99.7% of Alice's deposit,\nin two transactions, using only the documented owner API. No key compromise required;\nthis is what the role is currently allowed to do.\n\nTwo smaller variants, both also reproduced in that run:\n\n- `test_F4_FeeOf100PctBricksDeposits` — `setDepositFee(10_000)` makes every deposit\n  revert with `NoSharesMinted`.\n- `test_F4_FeeAbove100PctPanicsOnUnderflow` — anything above 10,000 reverts with an\n  arithmetic panic on `amount - fee` (line 88), since nothing constrains\n  `fee <= amount`.\n\n**Fix.** Three changes, all needed:\n\n1. **Cap the fee in the setter**, e.g. `if (newFeeBps > MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS) revert\n   FeeTooHigh();` with `MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS` a constant at a defensible level (100 bps\n   / 1%). Validate the constructor argument against the same bound — it is currently\n   unchecked too, so a vault can be *deployed* with a 100% fee. A cap well under\n   `BPS_DENOMINATOR` also removes both DoS variants for free.\n2. **Put the owner behind a timelock and a multisig.** A cap alone still lets a\n   compromised key take 1% of every deposit; a delay is what makes the change\n   observable before it lands.\n3. **Give `deposit` a slippage guard** — `deposit(uint256 amount, uint256 minShares)`,\n   reverting if fewer shares are minted. This protects depositors from any fee change\n   landing between transaction submission and inclusion, which is the actual attack\n   vector, and is standard for any vault entry point.\n\n---\n\n## F-5 — `pause()` freezes withdrawals, and the lock can be made permanent. Severity: Medium.\n\n**The bug.** `withdraw` carries `whenNotPaused` (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:107`). Pausing\nis meant to stop new risk from entering; here it also stops users getting out. There is\nno emergency-exit path that bypasses the pause, and no cap on how long a pause lasts.\n\nWorse, `Ownable` brings `renounceOwnership()`, which is callable while paused. Pausing\nand then renouncing sets the owner to `address(0)` — after which `unpause()` can never\nbe called by anyone. Every deposit is locked in the contract permanently. This needs no\nmalice; a fat-fingered `renounceOwnership()` during an incident response is enough.\n\n**Evidence** — `test_F5_PauseTrapsDepositorFunds` and\n`test_F5_PauseThenRenounceLocksFundsForever` in the `test/AuditAccounting.t.sol` output\nabove. The second shows two users deposit 10,000 USDT each, the owner pauses and\nrenounces, `unpause()` then reverts for every caller, Alice's `withdraw` reverts with\n`EnforcedPause`, and **20,000 USDT of aUSDT sits locked with no owner and no exit.**\n\nThe same property stated positively is `test_SPEC_PauseDoesNotBlockExit` in the spec\nsuite, which fails with `EnforcedPause()`.\n\n**Fix.** Remove `whenNotPaused` from `withdraw`. Pausing should block `deposit` only —\nusers must always be able to leave. If you want a circuit breaker that can also stop\nwithdrawals in a genuine emergency, make it a separate, explicitly time-boxed\nmechanism rather than the same flag as the deposit pause. Separately, override\n`renounceOwnership()` to revert; there is no scenario where this contract benefits from\nhaving no owner.\n\n---\n\n## Reproducing all of it\n\n```bash\nforge test                                    # everything\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditSpec.t.sol'        # the sign-off checklist: 6 red\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditFork.t.sol' -vv    # F-1, F-2 vs real mainnet\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditYield.t.sol' -vv   # F-2, no network needed\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditAccounting.t.sol' -vv   # F-3, F-4, F-5\nforge test --match-test 'invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone' --fuzz-seed 1\n```\n\nThe fork tests pin **mainnet block 25,600,000** and default to the public archive\nendpoint `https://eth.drpc.org`. If that is rate-limited, point them anywhere else:\n\n```bash\nMAINNET_RPC_URL=<your archive rpc> forge test --match-path 'test/AuditFork.t.sol' -vv\n```\n\nFull run as of this writing — 58 passing, 7 failing, where the 7 failures are the spec\nsuite and the leak invariant, and many of the 58 passes are exploits succeeding:\n\n```console\n$ forge test\nRan 6 test suites in 16.06s (30.45s CPU time): 58 tests passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped (65 total tests)\n```\n\n### Files I added\n\nEverything is new; nothing existing was edited.\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `test/AuditSpec.t.sol` | The six promised properties as assertions. Currently 0/6. |\n| `test/AuditFork.t.sol` | F-1 and F-2 against real USDT + real Aave V3, pinned block. |\n| `test/AuditYield.t.sol` | F-2 offline, via an aToken that actually accrues. |\n| `test/AuditAccounting.t.sol` | F-3, F-4, F-5 reproductions on the shipped mocks. |\n| `test/AuditInvariant.t.sol` | Invariant suite (the repo had none). |\n| `test/helpers/AccruingAavePool.sol` | Aave stand-in with a liquidity index. |\n\n`src/`, `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol`, and `test/mocks/` are byte-for-byte unchanged —\ntheir mtimes are still the checkout time, and the original 39 tests still pass:\n\n```console\n$ find src test -type f -name '*.sol' -exec stat -f '%Sm  %N' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' {} \\; | sort\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  src/interfaces/IAavePool.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  test/mocks/MockAavePool.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  test/mocks/MockUSDT.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:42:43  test/helpers/AccruingAavePool.sol\n2026-07-27 12:44:18  test/AuditAccounting.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:45:01  test/AuditYield.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:46:30  test/AuditFork.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:47:06  test/AuditInvariant.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:48:22  test/AuditSpec.t.sol\n```\n\n---\n\n## Lower-severity notes\n\nNot separately evidenced; flagged for the fix pass.\n\n- **`deposit` writes state after its external call** (`lines 95-99`). `nonReentrant`\n  makes this safe today, but it inverts checks-effects-interactions for no reason.\n  Move the three state updates above `aavePool.supply`.\n- **`aavePool.withdraw`'s return value is ignored** (`line 119`). Aave returns the\n  amount actually withdrawn. Assert it equals `netAssets` rather than assuming.\n- **`withdraw` can call Aave with `netAssets == 0`** for dust share amounts, where the\n  real pool reverts. `withdraw` guards `shares == 0` but not the resulting asset\n  amount.\n- **The `Withdrawn` event logs `netAssets` while `Deposited` logs the gross `amount`**\n  (`lines 101, 121`). Inconsistent, and it will quietly skew any off-chain accounting\n  built on these events.\n- **No slippage or deadline protection on either entry point**, beyond the `minShares`\n  argument recommended in F-4.\n- **Branch coverage is 85.71%, not 100%.** The one uncovered branch is worth finding\n  during the fix pass; the \"100%\" figure being circulated is lines and functions only.\n\n## What I would want before signing off\n\n1. F-1 through F-5 fixed — preferably by rebasing onto OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626`, which\n   removes the entire class of F-2 and F-3 rather than patching two symptoms.\n2. `test/AuditSpec.t.sol` green, all six.\n3. The invariant suite green, including `invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone`,\n   run at raised depth.\n4. A fork test that completes a full deposit → accrue → withdraw cycle against the real\n   USDT and the real Aave pool with **no** `vm.mockCall` anywhere in it. That single\n   test would have caught F-1 and F-2 on day one, and its absence is why 39 green tests\n   and 100% coverage told you nothing about whether this works.\n5. An external audit. F-4 in particular is a governance/key-management question as much\n   as a code one, and that deserves a second set of eyes on the deployment plan, not\n   just the contract.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2147,"cache_read_input_tokens":109703,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2147},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ef06dcc0-c456-4ae8-9b1a-06956807da6b","uuid":"6c24e059-1615-49aa-9a78-045a51ccc6e8","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:52:42.153Z","request_id":"req_011CdSGv1X1LStn8KKBdokzS"}

Every one reproduces against `src/` exactly as\nit stands today. Nothing under `src/`, `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol`, or `test/mocks/`\nwas modified — all new code is in new files.\n\n| # | Finding | Severity | Effect |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| F-1 | `deposit()` reverts against real USDT | **Critical** | Vault is 100% non-functional on mainnet |\n| F-2 | Aave interest never reaches the share price | **Critical** | Pays no yield; depositors lose the exit fee; yield is unrecoverable |\n| F-3 | Withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed | **High** | Value leaks out of the accounting on every withdrawal, permanently |\n| F-4 | `setDepositFee` is unbounded and instant | **Critical** | Owner can take ~99% of any incoming deposit |\n| F-5 | `pause()` also freezes `withdraw()` | **Medium** | Owner can trap all deposits; irreversible if ownership is renounced |\n\n---\n\n## Why the existing suite is green\n\nThe team's numbers are real. I reproduced them:\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol'\n[PASS] test_WithdrawReturnsUsdt() (gas: 196362)\nSuite result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 6.09ms (2.82ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 159.96ms (6.09ms CPU time): 39 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (39 total tests)\n```\n\n```console\n$ forge coverage --match-path 'test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol' --no-match-coverage 'test/'\n╭------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------+-----------------╮\n| File                   | % Lines         | % Statements   | % Branches   | % Funcs         |\n+============================================================================================+\n| src/UsdtYieldVault.sol | 100.00% (52/52) | 98.25% (56/57) | 85.71% (6/7) | 100.00% (11/11) |\n|------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------+-----------------|\n| Total                  | 100.00% (52/52) | 98.25% (56/57) | 85.71% (6/7) | 100.00% (11/11) |\n╰------------------------+-----------------+----------------+--------------+-----------------╯\n```\n\n100% of lines and 100% of functions, as claimed. The coverage number is not wrong —\nit is measuring the wrong thing. Coverage says *\"every line ran\"*. It cannot say\n*\"every line was right\"*, and two properties of the test doubles guarantee the bugs\nbelow can never be observed by this suite no matter how many tests are added to it:\n\n1. **`test/mocks/MockUSDT.sol` is a standard OpenZeppelin ERC20.** It returns `bool`\n   from `approve`. Real USDT does not. F-1 is invisible to every test that uses it.\n2. **`test/mocks/MockAavePool.sol` mints its receipt token 1:1 and has no liquidity\n   index** (`MockAavePool.sol:42-45`). It is structurally incapable of paying\n   interest, so no test using it can ever notice that the vault drops the interest\n   on the floor. F-2 and F-3 are invisible to it.\n\nThe mocks encode the same assumptions as the contract, so the suite agrees with the\ncontract about things they are both wrong about.\n\n---\n\n## The sign-off suite (`test/AuditSpec.t.sol`)\n\nBefore the individual findings, here is the shortest summary of the state of this\ncontract. `test/AuditSpec.t.sol` states, as assertions, six properties taken from\n`README.md` and the NatSpec on `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol`. It is the checklist I would\nwant green before this holds money. Today it is 0 for 6:\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditSpec.t.sol'\n\nRan 6 tests for test/AuditSpec.t.sol:AuditSpecTest\n[FAIL: a deposit must not lose more than a plausible fee: 1000000000 < 90000000000] test_SPEC_DepositFeeIsBounded() (gas: 309167)\n[FAIL: a year at 5% should leave the depositor up: 999700000000 <= 1000000000000] test_SPEC_DepositorIsNotWorseOffAfterAProfitableYear() (gas: 243893)\n[FAIL: nothing may be left behind once all shares are burned: 5999999 != 0] test_SPEC_NoValueBecomesUnreachable() (gas: 337133)\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_SPEC_PauseDoesNotBlockExit() (gas: 217537)\n[FAIL: bob must receive the fee alice paid: 1 !~= 3001500 (max delta: 1, real delta: 3001499)] test_SPEC_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() (gas: 324491)\n[FAIL: depositor's claim must grow with the yield: 100000000000 <= 100000000000] test_SPEC_YieldAccruesToDepositors() (gas: 228396)\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 6 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 2.93ms (930.75µs CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 161.22ms (2.93ms CPU time): 0 tests passed, 6 failed, 0 skipped (6 total tests)\n```\n\n---\n\n## F-1 — `deposit()` reverts against real USDT. Severity: Critical.\n\n**The bug.** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:93-94`:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nusdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\nLine 93 correctly uses `SafeERC20`. Line 94 does not — it calls `approve` through the\n`IERC20` interface, which ABI-decodes a `bool` from the return data. Real USDT's\n`approve` is declared with no return value and returns zero bytes, so the decode\nreverts. `SafeERC20` is imported and in scope; it was simply not used on this one line.\n\nThis is not a rare path. It is on the only code path into the vault. **Every deposit\nreverts. The contract cannot accept a single dollar.**\n\n**Evidence.** `test/AuditFork.t.sol`, forked at mainnet block 25,600,000 against the\nreal USDT and the real Aave V3 pool from `README.md`.\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditFork.t.sol' -vv\n\nRan 5 tests for test/AuditFork.t.sol:AuditForkTest\n[PASS] testFuzz_F1_NoDepositSizeSucceeds(uint256) (runs: 256, μ: 95563, ~: 95707)\n[PASS] test_F1_Control_RealAaveAcceptsUsdtSupplyDirectly() (gas: 205887)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT minted to alice by real Aave: 9999999999\n\n[PASS] test_F1_DepositAlwaysRevertsOnMainnet() (gas: 125016)\n[PASS] test_F1_RealUsdtApproveReturnsNoData() (gas: 150977)\nLogs:\n  raw USDT.approve call succeeded: true\n  USDT.approve return data length: 0\n\n[PASS] test_F2_RealAaveInterestIsStrandedAndDepositorLosesMoney() (gas: 327626)\nLogs:\n  principal supplied to Aave    : 1000000000000\n  aUSDT held after 365 days     : 1027640396805\n  real interest earned          : 27640396805\n  vault.totalAssets()           : 1000000000000\n  sharePrice at deposit         : 1001001\n  sharePrice after 365 days     : 1001001\n  alice received back           : 997000000000\n  alice net P&L                 : - 3000000000\n  aUSDT stranded in the vault   : 30640396804\n\nSuite result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 458.79ms (32.66ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 460.01ms (458.79ms CPU time): 5 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (5 total tests)\n```\n\nReading the four F-1 results:\n\n- `test_F1_RealUsdtApproveReturnsNoData` — real USDT's `approve` succeeds as a raw\n  call but returns **0 bytes**. The same call made through `IERC20` from a contract\n  frame reverts; the identical call against USDC on the same fork returns `true` fine.\n- `test_F1_DepositAlwaysRevertsOnMainnet` — `vault.deposit(10_000e6)` reverts, and\n  afterwards `totalShares == 0` and the vault holds no aUSDT.\n- `testFuzz_F1_NoDepositSizeSucceeds` — 256 fuzzed amounts from 1 USDT to 1M USDT.\n  Every one reverts. There is no working deposit size.\n- `test_F1_Control_RealAaveAcceptsUsdtSupplyDirectly` — the control. An EOA supplies\n  10,000 USDT straight into the real Aave pool at this block and gets aUSDT back. The\n  reserve is live and accepting deposits; the revert is the vault's fault, not Aave's.\n\nYou can also see it without Foundry at all:\n\n```console\n$ cast call 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 \"approve(address,uint256)\" \\\n    0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2 1000000 \\\n    --from 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001234 \\\n    --block 25600000 --rpc-url https://eth.drpc.org\n0x\n```\n\n`0x` is empty return data. A function declared `returns (bool)` cannot decode that.\n\n**Fix.** Use `SafeERC20` on line 94 as it is already used on line 93, and reset the\nallowance to zero before setting it:\n\n```solidity\nusdt.forceApprove(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\n`forceApprove` handles both USDT quirks: the missing return value, and USDT's\n`require(!((_value != 0) && (allowed[msg.sender][_spender] != 0)))`, which reverts on\nany non-zero-to-non-zero allowance change. The second quirk is latent today because\nAave consumes the full allowance on every `supply`, but it becomes a live bug the\nmoment `supply` ever pulls less than `amount` (e.g. a future Aave upgrade, or a\npartial supply), and it costs nothing to be safe about now.\n\nWorth noting for the wider review: the fact that this shipped means **nothing in this\nrepo has ever been executed against the real USDT contract.** F-1 is the cheapest bug\nhere to fix and the loudest signal about process.\n\n---\n\n## F-2 — Aave interest never reaches the share price. Severity: Critical.\n\n**The bug.** `totalAssets()` (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:143-145`) returns\n`totalAssetsStored`, a plain counter. Grepping every mention in `src/`:\n\n```console\n$ grep -rn \"totalAssetsStored\" src/\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:53:    uint256 public totalAssetsStored;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:97:        totalAssetsStored += amount;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:117:        totalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:144:        return totalAssetsStored;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:154:        return assets.mulDiv(totalShares, totalAssetsStored);\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:164:        return shares.mulDiv(totalAssetsStored, totalShares);\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:175:        return totalAssetsStored.mulDiv(1e18, totalShares);\n```\n\nIt moves in exactly two places: `deposit` and `withdraw`. Nothing else can change it —\nand interest arriving from Aave is not a deposit or a withdrawal. Meanwhile the aUSDT\nbalance that actually represents the vault's position is never read:\n\n```console\n$ grep -rn \"aUsdt\" src/\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:41:    IERC20 public immutable aUsdt;\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:68:    /// @param _aUsdt The Aave aUSDT receipt token.\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:72:    constructor(address _usdt, address _aUsdt, address _aavePool, uint256 _depositFeeBps, address initialOwner)\nsrc/UsdtYieldVault.sol:76:        aUsdt = IERC20(_aUsdt);\n```\n\n`aUsdt` is assigned in the constructor and **never read again**. That dead immutable\nis the shape of the missing feature: the vault holds a rebasing token and never looks\nat it. The share price is frozen at deployment. This is a yield vault that does not\npay yield.\n\n**Evidence, against the real Aave V3 pool.** In\n`test_F2_RealAaveInterestIsStrandedAndDepositorLosesMoney` (output pasted under F-1\nabove) a depositor supplies 1,000,000 USDT, a year passes, and:\n\n| | USDT |\n|---|---|\n| Real interest Aave paid the vault's position | **27,640.40** |\n| `vault.totalAssets()` after that year | 1,000,000.00 — unchanged |\n| `sharePrice()` before / after | 1001001 / 1001001 — unchanged |\n| Depositor received on exit | 997,000.00 |\n| **Depositor's P&L on a year at ~2.76%** | **−3,000.00** |\n| aUSDT left stranded in the vault | **30,640.40** |\n\nThe depositor is *down three thousand dollars* on a position that earned twenty-seven\nthousand. They pay the 0.3% exit fee and receive none of the yield.\n\nNote this test has to patch F-1 to run at all — it `vm.mockCall`s **only the return\nvalue of `USDT.approve`** and pre-sets the real allowance, so execution can get past\nline 94. The vault, USDT, the Aave pool, and the interest rate are all real and\nunmodified. Everything after line 94 is the contract as it stands.\n\n**Same result without any network access**, using an aToken that has a liquidity index\nthe way real aUSDT does (`test/helpers/AccruingAavePool.sol` — a new file; the shipped\nmock is untouched):\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditYield.t.sol' -vv\n\nRan 3 tests for test/AuditYield.t.sol:AuditYieldTest\n[PASS] testFuzz_F2_SharePriceIgnoresAnyAmountOfInterest(uint256,uint256) (runs: 256, μ: 189212, ~: 189529)\n[PASS] test_F2_DepositorLosesMoneyDespitePositiveYield() (gas: 198897)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited              : 100000000000\n  alice received back          : 99700000000\n  alice net P&L                : - 300000000\n  interest the position earned : 5000000000\n  aUSDT stranded in the vault  : 5300000000\n\n[PASS] test_F2_InterestNeverReachesTheSharePrice() (gas: 202682)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT the vault really holds : 105000000000\n  vault.totalAssets()          : 100000000000\n  sharePrice before accrual    : 1001001\n  sharePrice after  accrual    : 1001001\n  alice redeemable before      : 100000000000\n  alice redeemable after       : 100000000000\n\nSuite result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 15.75ms (15.52ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 167.80ms (15.75ms CPU time): 3 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (3 total tests)\n```\n\n`testFuzz_F2_SharePriceIgnoresAnyAmountOfInterest` fuzzes 256 combinations of\nprincipal and yield from 0.01% to 100%. The share price does not move for any of them.\n\n**The yield is not merely uncredited — it is unrecoverable.** There is no function on\nthis contract that can move it:\n\n```console\n$ forge inspect UsdtYieldVault abi --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.type==\"function\") | .name' | sort\naavePool\naUsdt\nbalanceOfUnderlying\nBPS_DENOMINATOR\nconvertToAssets\nconvertToShares\ndeposit\ndepositFeeBps\nMIN_DEPOSIT\nowner\npause\npaused\nrenounceOwnership\nsetDepositFee\nSHARE_SCALE\nshareBalance\nsharePrice\ntotalAssets\ntotalAssetsStored\ntotalShares\ntransferOwnership\nunpause\nusdt\nWITHDRAW_FEE_BPS\nwithdraw\n```\n\nNo sweep, no rescue, no `skim`, no emergency withdrawal, and the contract is not\nupgradeable. `withdraw` can only ever pay out against `totalAssetsStored`, which never\ncounts the interest. Once all shares are burned, `totalShares` returns to 0 and a new\ndepositor mints at the flat rate — they do not inherit it either. **Every dollar of\nyield this vault ever earns is permanently destroyed.**\n\n**Fix.** Make `totalAssets()` a measurement rather than a counter:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\nand delete `totalAssetsStored` along with its two updates, routing `convertToShares` /\n`convertToAssets` / `sharePrice` through `totalAssets()`. aUSDT is rebasing, so its\n`balanceOf` *is* principal plus accrued interest, which is exactly the quantity the\nshare price should track. This is also the fix for F-3 below — the two bugs share a\nroot cause, which is that the contract keeps its own books instead of reading Aave's.\n\nTwo things to handle when you do this:\n\n- Switching to a balance-based `totalAssets()` re-opens the classic ERC-4626 inflation\n  attack, which the stored counter incidentally blocked (a direct aUSDT donation\n  currently does nothing). Mitigate with virtual shares/assets — OpenZeppelin's\n  `ERC4626` does this by default with a decimals offset.\n- Strongly consider inheriting OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626` outright instead of\n  hand-rolling shares. It gets the rounding directions, the inflation defence, and the\n  conversion maths right, and it would have prevented F-2, F-3, and the rounding\n  surface entirely.\n\n---\n\n## F-3 — The withdrawal fee is destroyed, not redistributed. Severity: High.\n\n**The bug.** `README.md` states:\n\n> Both fees stay supplied in Aave and accrue to the remaining shareholders — they are\n> not swept to the owner.\n\nThe deposit fee does behave that way. The withdrawal fee does not.\n`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:111-119`:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 grossAssets = convertToAssets(shares);\nuint256 fee = (grossAssets * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;\nnetAssets = grossAssets - fee;\n...\ntotalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;      // <-- gross\naavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);   // <-- net\n```\n\n`grossAssets` is subtracted from the books but only `netAssets` leaves Aave. The fee\nis simultaneously removed from the accounting *and* left sitting in Aave. It belongs\nto nobody. The share price for the remaining holders is unchanged, so they receive\nnone of it — the exact opposite of what the README promises. To redistribute the fee\nthe line must subtract `netAssets`, leaving the fee inside `totalAssetsStored` where\nthe remaining shares divide it.\n\n**Evidence.**\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-path 'test/AuditAccounting.t.sol' -vv\n\nRan 8 tests for test/AuditAccounting.t.sol:AuditAccountingTest\n[PASS] testFuzz_F3_EveryWithdrawFeeIsStranded(uint256,uint256,uint256) (runs: 256, μ: 279834, ~: 279941)\n[PASS] test_F3_StrandedValueIsPermanentlyUnrecoverable() (gas: 392700)\nLogs:\n  all shares burned; totalShares       : 0\n  vault.totalAssets()                  : 0\n  aUSDT left in the vault forever      : 5999999\n\n[PASS] test_F3_WithdrawFeeIsDestroyedNotRedistributed() (gas: 283604)\nLogs:\n  alice paid withdraw fee (USDT base units): 3001500\n  bob's redeemable value gained         : 1\n  aUSDT actually held by vault          : 1002501250\n  vault.totalAssets() (booked)          : 999499750\n  stranded, owned by nobody             : 3001500\n\n[PASS] test_F4_FeeAbove100PctPanicsOnUnderflow() (gas: 28631)\n[PASS] test_F4_FeeOf100PctBricksDeposits() (gas: 30588)\n[PASS] test_F4_OwnerSandwichesDepositAndTakesThePrincipal() (gas: 288745)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited                : 100000000000\n  alice can redeem               : 1000000000\n  owner deposited                : 1000000000\n  owner can redeem               : 100000000000\n  owner net profit (USDT units)  : 99700000000\n\n[PASS] test_F5_PauseThenRenounceLocksFundsForever() (gas: 275236)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT locked with no owner and no exit: 20000000000\n\n[PASS] test_F5_PauseTrapsDepositorFunds() (gas: 197407)\nSuite result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 29.58ms (30.34ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 160.06ms (29.58ms CPU time): 8 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (8 total tests)\n```\n\nThese tests assert the *buggy* behaviour, so a green tick here means the bug\nreproduces exactly as described. In `test_F3_WithdrawFeeIsDestroyedNotRedistributed`,\nAlice pays a **3.0015 USDT** withdrawal fee; Bob, the sole remaining shareholder and\nthe person the README promises it to, gains **1 base unit** (0.000001 USDT — pure\nrounding). The vault ends up holding 1002.501250 USDT of aUSDT against booked assets of\n999.499750 — a gap of **3.0015 USDT, exactly Alice's fee**.\n\n`testFuzz_F3_EveryWithdrawFeeIsStranded` fuzzes 256 combinations of two deposit sizes\nand a withdrawal percentage and asserts the gap grows by precisely the fee every time.\nThis is not a rounding artefact; it is the full fee, on every withdrawal, forever.\n\n`test_F3_StrandedValueIsPermanentlyUnrecoverable` runs the vault to completion: after\nboth users exit, `totalShares == 0` and `totalAssets() == 0`, but **5.999999 USDT of\nreal aUSDT remains** with no owner and no function that can reach it (see the ABI dump\nunder F-2). A fresh depositor then mints at the flat rate and does not inherit it.\n\n**Also caught by an invariant.** The shipped suite has no invariant tests at all;\n`test/AuditInvariant.t.sol` adds them. The property \"every asset the vault holds is\nclaimable by some shareholder\" fails and shrinks to a **two-call** counterexample —\none deposit, one withdrawal:\n\n```console\n$ forge test --match-test 'invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone' --fuzz-seed 1\n\nRan 1 test for test/AuditInvariant.t.sol:AuditInvariantTest\n[FAIL: vault holds aUSDT that no share can ever redeem: 190812277685 != 190726906501]\n\t[Sequence] (original: 10, shrunk: 2)\n\t\tsender=0x000000000000000000000000000000000000067C addr=[test/AuditInvariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=deposit(uint256,uint256) args=[1, 100450808277457133411089551021215742859610800683149140176168249 [1.004e62]]\n\t\tsender=0xAc5AFbbb4a2A0b07D8bF6DcA0a463F25a89a0852 addr=[test/AuditInvariant.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=withdraw(uint256,uint256) args=[4332493505980643184868765250267057563298485427723145276166 [4.332e57], 56163704696640452142197199127252104166317009532074502048454053802634565426 [5.616e73]]\n invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone() (runs: 0, calls: 0, reverts: 0)\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 5.57ms (4.75ms CPU time)\n```\n\n`--fuzz-seed 1` pins the sequence so you get these exact numbers. Without it the test\nstill always fails, but the shrunk sequence and figures will differ run to run — if\nyou want a fully deterministic repro of the same accounting, use\n`test_F3_WithdrawFeeIsDestroyedNotRedistributed` above.\n\nTwo neighbouring invariants in that file **pass**, and they matter for scoping this\ncorrectly:\n\n- `invariant_VaultIsNeverUnderReserved` — the vault always holds *at least* what its\n  books claim. It is over-reserved, not insolvent. Withdrawals will not fail for lack\n  of funds.\n- `invariant_TotalSharesRedeemValueLteTotalAssets` — rounding never lets holders\n  redeem more than the books say.\n\nSo F-3 is a leak, not a bank run. Nobody can steal the stranded value; everybody\nloses it.\n\n**Fix.** Change `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:117` to subtract the net amount:\n\n```solidity\ntotalAssetsStored -= netAssets;\n```\n\nThis leaves the fee inside the accounting so it accretes to the remaining shares,\nwhich is what the README describes. If you adopt the F-2 fix and make `totalAssets()`\nread `aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this))`, this bug disappears on its own — the fee stays\nin the measured balance and is automatically shared. Prefer that; fixing F-2 and F-3\nseparately is fixing the same root cause twice.\n\n---\n\n## F-4 — `setDepositFee` is unbounded and takes effect instantly. Severity: Critical.\n\n**The bug.** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:126-130` accepts any `uint256` with no cap, no\ntimelock, and no delay. The fee is not collected as a transfer — it shrinks the shares\nminted (`line 90`) while the **full** deposit is still credited to `totalAssetsStored`\n(`line 97`). Raising the fee therefore transfers the incoming depositor's principal to\nwhoever already holds shares. The owner is free to be that holder.\n\n**Evidence** — `test_F4_OwnerSandwichesDepositAndTakesThePrincipal` in the\n`test/AuditAccounting.t.sol` output above. The owner stakes 1,000 USDT, front-runs a\nvictim's deposit by calling `setDepositFee(9_999)`, and:\n\n| | USDT in | Redeemable after |\n|---|---|---|\n| Alice (victim) | 100,000 | **1,000** |\n| Owner | 1,000 | **100,000** |\n\nThe owner then exits with a net profit of **99,700 USDT** — 99.7% of Alice's deposit,\nin two transactions, using only the documented owner API. No key compromise required;\nthis is what the role is currently allowed to do.\n\nTwo smaller variants, both also reproduced in that run:\n\n- `test_F4_FeeOf100PctBricksDeposits` — `setDepositFee(10_000)` makes every deposit\n  revert with `NoSharesMinted`.\n- `test_F4_FeeAbove100PctPanicsOnUnderflow` — anything above 10,000 reverts with an\n  arithmetic panic on `amount - fee` (line 88), since nothing constrains\n  `fee <= amount`.\n\n**Fix.** Three changes, all needed:\n\n1. **Cap the fee in the setter**, e.g. `if (newFeeBps > MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS) revert\n   FeeTooHigh();` with `MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS` a constant at a defensible level (100 bps\n   / 1%). Validate the constructor argument against the same bound — it is currently\n   unchecked too, so a vault can be *deployed* with a 100% fee. A cap well under\n   `BPS_DENOMINATOR` also removes both DoS variants for free.\n2. **Put the owner behind a timelock and a multisig.** A cap alone still lets a\n   compromised key take 1% of every deposit; a delay is what makes the change\n   observable before it lands.\n3. **Give `deposit` a slippage guard** — `deposit(uint256 amount, uint256 minShares)`,\n   reverting if fewer shares are minted. This protects depositors from any fee change\n   landing between transaction submission and inclusion, which is the actual attack\n   vector, and is standard for any vault entry point.\n\n---\n\n## F-5 — `pause()` freezes withdrawals, and the lock can be made permanent. Severity: Medium.\n\n**The bug.** `withdraw` carries `whenNotPaused` (`src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:107`). Pausing\nis meant to stop new risk from entering; here it also stops users getting out. There is\nno emergency-exit path that bypasses the pause, and no cap on how long a pause lasts.\n\nWorse, `Ownable` brings `renounceOwnership()`, which is callable while paused. Pausing\nand then renouncing sets the owner to `address(0)` — after which `unpause()` can never\nbe called by anyone. Every deposit is locked in the contract permanently. This needs no\nmalice; a fat-fingered `renounceOwnership()` during an incident response is enough.\n\n**Evidence** — `test_F5_PauseTrapsDepositorFunds` and\n`test_F5_PauseThenRenounceLocksFundsForever` in the `test/AuditAccounting.t.sol` output\nabove. The second shows two users deposit 10,000 USDT each, the owner pauses and\nrenounces, `unpause()` then reverts for every caller, Alice's `withdraw` reverts with\n`EnforcedPause`, and **20,000 USDT of aUSDT sits locked with no owner and no exit.**\n\nThe same property stated positively is `test_SPEC_PauseDoesNotBlockExit` in the spec\nsuite, which fails with `EnforcedPause()`.\n\n**Fix.** Remove `whenNotPaused` from `withdraw`. Pausing should block `deposit` only —\nusers must always be able to leave. If you want a circuit breaker that can also stop\nwithdrawals in a genuine emergency, make it a separate, explicitly time-boxed\nmechanism rather than the same flag as the deposit pause. Separately, override\n`renounceOwnership()` to revert; there is no scenario where this contract benefits from\nhaving no owner.\n\n---\n\n## Reproducing all of it\n\n```bash\nforge test                                    # everything\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditSpec.t.sol'        # the sign-off checklist: 6 red\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditFork.t.sol' -vv    # F-1, F-2 vs real mainnet\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditYield.t.sol' -vv   # F-2, no network needed\nforge test --match-path 'test/AuditAccounting.t.sol' -vv   # F-3, F-4, F-5\nforge test --match-test 'invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone' --fuzz-seed 1\n```\n\nThe fork tests pin **mainnet block 25,600,000** and default to the public archive\nendpoint `https://eth.drpc.org`. If that is rate-limited, point them anywhere else:\n\n```bash\nMAINNET_RPC_URL=<your archive rpc> forge test --match-path 'test/AuditFork.t.sol' -vv\n```\n\nFull run as of this writing — 58 passing, 7 failing, where the 7 failures are the spec\nsuite and the leak invariant, and many of the 58 passes are exploits succeeding:\n\n```console\n$ forge test\nRan 6 test suites in 16.06s (30.45s CPU time): 58 tests passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped (65 total tests)\n```\n\n### Files I added\n\nEverything is new; nothing existing was edited.\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `test/AuditSpec.t.sol` | The six promised properties as assertions. Currently 0/6. |\n| `test/AuditFork.t.sol` | F-1 and F-2 against real USDT + real Aave V3, pinned block. |\n| `test/AuditYield.t.sol` | F-2 offline, via an aToken that actually accrues. |\n| `test/AuditAccounting.t.sol` | F-3, F-4, F-5 reproductions on the shipped mocks. |\n| `test/AuditInvariant.t.sol` | Invariant suite (the repo had none). |\n| `test/helpers/AccruingAavePool.sol` | Aave stand-in with a liquidity index. |\n\n`src/`, `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol`, and `test/mocks/` are byte-for-byte unchanged —\ntheir mtimes are still the checkout time, and the original 39 tests still pass:\n\n```console\n$ find src test -type f -name '*.sol' -exec stat -f '%Sm  %N' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' {} \\; | sort\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  src/interfaces/IAavePool.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  test/mocks/MockAavePool.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  test/mocks/MockUSDT.sol\n2026-07-27 12:36:55  test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:42:43  test/helpers/AccruingAavePool.sol\n2026-07-27 12:44:18  test/AuditAccounting.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:45:01  test/AuditYield.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:46:30  test/AuditFork.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:47:06  test/AuditInvariant.t.sol\n2026-07-27 12:48:22  test/AuditSpec.t.sol\n```\n\n---\n\n## Lower-severity notes\n\nNot separately evidenced; flagged for the fix pass.\n\n- **`deposit` writes state after its external call** (`lines 95-99`). `nonReentrant`\n  makes this safe today, but it inverts checks-effects-interactions for no reason.\n  Move the three state updates above `aavePool.supply`.\n- **`aavePool.withdraw`'s return value is ignored** (`line 119`). Aave returns the\n  amount actually withdrawn. Assert it equals `netAssets` rather than assuming.\n- **`withdraw` can call Aave with `netAssets == 0`** for dust share amounts, where the\n  real pool reverts. `withdraw` guards `shares == 0` but not the resulting asset\n  amount.\n- **The `Withdrawn` event logs `netAssets` while `Deposited` logs the gross `amount`**\n  (`lines 101, 121`). Inconsistent, and it will quietly skew any off-chain accounting\n  built on these events.\n- **No slippage or deadline protection on either entry point**, beyond the `minShares`\n  argument recommended in F-4.\n- **Branch coverage is 85.71%, not 100%.** The one uncovered branch is worth finding\n  during the fix pass; the \"100%\" figure being circulated is lines and functions only.\n\n## What I would want before signing off\n\n1. F-1 through F-5 fixed — preferably by rebasing onto OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626`, which\n   removes the entire class of F-2 and F-3 rather than patching two symptoms.\n2. `test/AuditSpec.t.sol` green, all six.\n3. The invariant suite green, including `invariant_EveryAssetHeldIsClaimableBySomeone`,\n   run at raised depth.\n4. A fork test that completes a full deposit → accrue → withdraw cycle against the real\n   USDT and the real Aave pool with **no** `vm.mockCall` anywhere in it. That single\n   test would have caught F-1 and F-2 on day one, and its absence is why 39 green tests\n   and 100% coverage told you nothing about whether this works.\n5. An external audit. F-4 in particular is a governance/key-management question as much\n   as a code one, and that deserves a second set of eyes on the deployment plan, not\n   just the contract.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
